newsitem.title: USA: Mobil Corp. says in talks to link refining units.
newsitem.headline: Mobil Corp. says in talks to link refining units.

text.p: NEW YORK - Mobil Corp. said Monday it was negotiating with several companies on a possible deal to link its refining and marketing operations but declined to comment on a report it was discussing a merger of those businesses with Amoco Corp.

"We are continually looking to improve marketing and refining in the U.S. We have had and continue to have discussions with several, and I emphasise the word 'several,' companies," said Mobil spokesman Christopher Springham.
"None has reached the stage where it is possible to reach any conclusions," he said.

Springham would not comment directly on a story in the business section of the Sunday Telegraph, a London newspaper, which quoted unidentified sources that said Mobil was "deep in talks" with Chicago-based Amoco to merge their refining and marketing operations in the United States and overseas.
The newspaper article speculated the deal would involve around $20 billion of assets.
Amoco officials were not immediately available for comment.
Wall Street seemed to welcome such a linkup. Mobil's stock jumped $1.875 to $136, and Amoco gained $2.125 to $86.875 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
Global merger fever has swept the industry over the past couple of years.
Fairfax, Va.-based Mobil and BP America Inc., the U.S. unit of British Petroleum Co. Plc agreed about 18 months ago to link their European refining and marketing interests.
Last year Shell Oil Co. and Texaco Inc. agreed to merge their U.S. interests, including Texaco's joint venture with Saudi Aramco, Star Enterprises.
In the United States, nine out of the top 25 refiners have been involved over the past year in mergers, acquisitions or "alliances" and the industry is rife with rumours of more deals.

There were rumours last week that Mobil and BP America were negotiating a merger of their U.S. refining and marketing assets after Marathon Oil Co. and Ashland Inc. agreed to link their U.S. refining and marketing businesses in a 62/38 percent split.
Amoco has said several times that it is seeking a partner for its downstream assets, and analysts say Atlantic Richfield Co. and Sun Co. are looking to hook up with a U.S. partner.

A marriage of Amoco and Mobil's operations would link the No. 3 and No. 5 U.S. refiners with combined capacity to process nearly 2 million barrels per day of crude oil, according to the worldwide refinery survey by the Oil & Gas Journal, a trade magazine.
Amoco and Mobil both have large refineries in the South and Midwest. Mobil has medium-sized plants on the East and West Coasts and in Louisiana.
Amoco also has large Texas and Indiana refineries and a smattering of plants from Virginia to Utah.
